title: Road to Wiki Cohort 2 — 30+ Wikimedia Patches, 3 Awards | Gautam Kumar Maurya
description: A field ledger of the WikiClub Tech India × OKI IIIT Hyderabad Road to Wiki Cohort 2 fellowship: three phases across eight to nine months, 30+ merged Wikimedia patches, a fully funded Vande Bharat journey to Gurugram and three graduation awards — Best Contributor, Most Active Contributor and 1st Rank.

programme.name: Road to Wiki — Cohort 2
programme.location: Online (Google Meet) · Graduation at Gurugram, Haryana, India
programme.role: Cohort 2 fellow · WikiClub Tech campus envoy
programme.outcome: 30+ merged Wikimedia patches, eight of them featured in the WikiClub Tech Technical Impact Report I (Jan–Jun 2026), and three awards presented at the national conclave in Gurugram, 2–4 October 2026.

phases.name: Induction & technical foundations

Git, CI/CD, SSH and Phabricator masterclass with Pratik Singh (GitLab), Aditya and Agamya.

Selected as GDG Prayagraj Community Volunteer 2026–27 under Ankit Sir and Mohd Shadab Sir.
phases.gate: First patchset pushed to Wikimedia Gerrit.

phases.name: The upstream marathon & systems
highlights: 1st position, 1-Week Wiki Contribution Marathon (20–27 April 2026), during college sessional exams.
High-scale systems session: SQL vs NoSQL, Elasticsearch, Redis and Varnish with Vrijraj Singh and Ankit Sir.
RTW-P2S3 engineering-growth session with Santhosh Thottingal (WMF Principal Software Engineer).
Joined the Universal Code of Conduct sync live from an auto rickshaw while commuting home.
8 upstream patches featured in the IIIT Hyderabad Technical Impact Report I.

phases.name: Wikispeech, Proofread & translatewiki
highlights: Group 3 kickoff led by Sarthak Singh, Shivaansh Singh and Dev Jadiya.
Proofread Tool (Wikisource): OCR corrections, digitisation and transcription UX.
translatewiki.net: localisation tooling, i18n notifications and Indic wiki support.
Wikispeech accessibility work on top of crossing 30+ merged patches.
Keynote speaker at Open Source Day, UIT Prayagraj — speaking to 100+ juniors.

dispatches.title: Selected as GDG Prayagraj Community Volunteer 2026–27
dispatches.quote: Last year I also applied but wasn't selected. Instead of stopping there, I kept learning, improving and staying connected with the community — and this time it worked.

dispatches.title: Mastering Git, SSH, CI/CD and Phabricator workflows
dispatches.quote: Over the past few sessions I got to dive deep into open source and developer workflows through Road to Wiki. Gained clarity, confidence and motivation to contribute actively.

dispatches.title: First position in the one-week WikiClub Tech contribution marathon
dispatches.quote: During this journey I explored real open-source workflows using Gerrit, Phabricator and Git. Managing this during college sessional exams taught me consistency, time management and dedication.

dispatches.title: SQL vs NoSQL and how Wikimedia handles distributed traffic
dispatches.quote: One of the most engaging technical sessions — database design, SQL vs NoSQL trade-offs, Redis caching, Elasticsearch indexing and how Wikimedia handles massive distributed traffic.

dispatches.title: Engineering growth with Santhosh Thottingal — and live praise
dispatches.quote: Participated in RTW-P2S3 on open source contributions to engineering growth. A special highlight was Ankit Sir publicly appreciating my contributions live during the session.

dispatches.title: Foundations of open source and code review with Sanskar Dubey
dispatches.quote: A crystal-clear understanding of how open-source communities work, review culture, and how contributors make meaningful impact through patient Gerrit workflows.

dispatches.title: The two-hour developer masterclass: Gerrit, SSH and workflows
dispatches.quote: A power-packed two-hour technical deep-dive into FOSS fundamentals, Gerrit code reviews, git rebases, SSH key setup and Phabricator project boards.

dispatches.title: Eight patches published in the WikiClub Tech Impact Report I
dispatches.quote: Honored to share that my open-source contributions have been officially recognized in the Technical Impact Report (Jan–June 2026) published by OKI at IIIT Hyderabad — eight production patches.

dispatches.title: Authoring upstream patches and passing CI/CD in MediaWiki
dispatches.quote: Working directly with Wikimedia Gerrit, passing automated Jenkins pipelines, resolving reviewer comments and ensuring backward compatibility across high-traffic MediaWiki codebases.

dispatches.title: Certificate of Achievement for 1st rank in the Wiki Marathon
dispatches.quote: Honored to receive the official Certificate of Achievement for securing 1st position in the Wiki Contribution Marathon 2026, organized by WikiClub Tech–UIT.

dispatches.title: Joining the Universal Code of Conduct sync live from an auto
dispatches.quote: While returning home from college I received the link for the UCoC sync and joined immediately — even while travelling in an auto. Community values, safety and mutual respect matter wherever you are.

dispatches.title: Speaking on open source at UIT Prayagraj to 100+ juniors
dispatches.quote: Organized by WikiClub Tech–UIT with GDG on Campus. After securing 1st rank, speaking to 100+ students about how open source really works, how to get started, and why real-world code matters.

dispatches.title: Phase 3 begins: advanced Wikimedia tooling
dispatches.quote: Working on real Wikimedia tools — Wikispeech, Proofread Tool (Wikisource) and translatewiki.net. A massive shift from learning to architecting upstream tools.

dispatches.title: Graduation 2026: Best Contributor, Vande Bharat and three awards
dispatches.quote: Eight to ten months culminating in Gurugram. Travelling from Prayagraj on the Vande Bharat Express for this fully funded conclave. Won three awards — Best Contributor and Most Active Contributor — and finally met Dev, Anushka, Tejinder, Pushpit, Shrey, Kavaljeet, Hridyesh, Shivaansh, Harsh, Adarsh, Arohi, Priyanshika, Neelima, Sanskar and Ankit Sir in person.

faq.q: What is Road to Wiki Cohort 2?
faq.a: Road to Wiki is the flagship technical program of WikiClub Tech India, run with the Open Knowledge Initiatives (OKI) at IIIT Hyderabad and supported by the Wikimedia Foundation. Cohort 2 brought 90+ students from 12 partner universities through three phases across 8–9 months — from January to the October 2026 graduation in Gurugram.

faq.q: How many upstream patches did you merge?
faq.a: 30+ across Wikimedia repositories. Eight were featured in the WikiClub Tech Technical Impact Report I (January–June 2026), spanning Pywikibot, the Function Orchestrator, MinervaNeue, GrowthExperiments, MediaWiki core, UploadWizard and ProofreadPage. The patch ledger on the page links each one.

faq.q: Which awards did you win at graduation?
faq.a: Three: Best Contributor, Most Active Contributor, and 1st Rank in the one-week WikiClub Tech marathon. All three were presented at the conclave in Gurugram on 2–4 October 2026.

faq.q: How can I verify the contributions independently?
faq.a: Every patch sits on the Wikimedia Gerrit under owner:gkm563, tasks appear on Phabricator as Gkm563, and the program record lives on Meta under IIITH-OKI/Wikiclub Tech/Road To Wiki, including the Contribution Ledger and The Celebration Day pages.

faq.q: What does “a community is a loop, not a line” mean?
faq.a: Learners enter, grow into contributors, and the strongest return as mentors for the next cohort. I crossed that loop during Cohort 2 and now mentor juniors at United Institute of Technology, Prayagraj, as a WikiClub Tech campus envoy.
